citation.authors: Srivarathan A, Bradford A, Shearkhani S, Heimlich L et al

cited_by.title: Autism and ADHD: being missed, delayed or misdiagnosed

record.population: 20 US studies of inequities in diagnosing mental disorders; 17 were about autism
record.design: Systematic review with narrative synthesis, studies 2015-2024, quality appraisal with the Mixed-Methods Appraisal Tool; studies of varying quality
record.finding: Most diagnostic errors were delayed diagnosis. Eleven factors contributed: limited health literacy was the leading cause in recognising symptoms, insurance coverage delayed engagement, provider bias during history-taking was a key cause of delays and misdiagnoses, and culturally inequivalent assessment measures might cause misdiagnosis and delayed diagnosis for Black/African American and Hispanic/Latino people.
record.note: US only; studies of varying methodological quality; mostly autism, so it says little about ADHD or bipolar.
